control_failures.control_label: benching, battering or shoring of an excavation
inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters

hazard_media: stored potential of an elevated component
facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: near hit during a planned shutdown on EX-9101

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EXCAVATION_SUPPORT: the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

Control GROUND_CONDITION_INSPECTION: the inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters was never verified as effective, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control SLOPE_MONITORING_RESPONSE: the response to slope monitoring alarms had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next spot check that the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation on EX-9101 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in designing and controlling excavations, specifically working near an unsupported edge. EX-9101 (earthmoving fleet) is in service for loading and dozing. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent. The gravity energy involved is held as suspended load, and the recorded presentation was fall, collapse, crush.
response.summary: On 22 October 2008 a near hit was recorded on EX-9101 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during a planned shutdown; gravity energy held as suspended load was not released.
